primary_growing_regions: Iran, Turkey, Spain, USA (California, Arizona), Israel

top_varieties_india.name: Bhagwa (Sinduri)
top_varieties_india.characteristics: Bright red rind, soft seeds, sweet, 20-28 Brix, most commercially grown

top_varieties_india.name: Ganesh
top_varieties_india.characteristics: Pinkish-white rind, soft seeds, 16-18 Brix, disease susceptible

top_varieties_india.name: Super Bhagwa
top_varieties_india.characteristics: Improved Bhagwa, larger fruits, more uniform

top_varieties_india.name: Arakta
top_varieties_india.characteristics: Blood-red arils, hard seeds, good keeping quality

top_varieties_india.name: Phule Arakta
top_varieties_india.characteristics: NRC Solapur release, tolerant to bacterial blight

phenology.description: Pomegranate is a deciduous to semi-evergreen tree/large shrub. Under Indian conditions, it can bear fruit 2-3 times a year with regulated cropping through stress-induced dormancy (bahar treatment).

bahar_system.description: Bahar is a unique pomegranate cropping system practiced in India. Trees are stressed (water withheld + leaf stripping) to synchronize flowering.

ambe_bahar.advantages: Best fruit quality, highest yield, less bacterial blight
ambe_bahar.disadvantages: Fruit susceptible to sun-scorch in some regions

mrig_bahar.disadvantages: High bacterial blight risk during monsoon flowering
mrig_bahar.recommended_regions: Irrigated areas only if disease can be managed

hasta_bahar.advantages: Winter fruit fetches premium price, low disease pressure
hasta_bahar.disadvantages: Lower yield, needs irrigation, frost risk in north India

bahar_treatment_protocol.step_1_stress: Withhold irrigation for 30-45 days after last harvest
bahar_treatment_protocol.step_2_ethrel: Apply Ethrel 1500-2000 ppm spray for uniform defoliation (optional)
bahar_treatment_protocol.step_4_rest: Allow tree to rest 15-20 days (bare canopy)
bahar_treatment_protocol.step_5_resume_irrigation: Resume drip irrigation + apply basal fertilizer dose
bahar_treatment_protocol.step_6_flowering: New shoots and flower buds emerge in 20-30 days

rest_pruning.description: Dormancy period after bahar treatment. No leaves. Minimal metabolic activity.

vegetative.description: New shoot flush after dormancy break. Rapid vegetative growth. Critical nitrogen window.

fertilizer.notes: High nitrogen for canopy development. Apply through drip/fertigate.

flowering.description: Flower bud initiation to full bloom. CRITICAL stage — nitrogen must be reduced to promote fruit set over vegetative growth.

types_of_flowers.hermaphrodite_vase: Productive — forms fruit. Bell/vase shaped. Keep these.
types_of_flowers.male_tubular: Non-productive — falls off. Narrow tubular shape.
types_of_flowers.intermediate: Partially productive, may set small fruit.

flowering.irrigation: Reduce to 10-15 L/tree/day — slight stress improves fruit set

fertilizer.avoid: AVOID high nitrogen — causes flower drop and excessive vegetative growth
fertilizer.notes: Boron is CRITICAL for pollen viability and fruit set. Calcium prevents cracking.

flowering.robot_action: DOSE — phosphorus + potassium + boron, NO nitrogen

fruiting.description: Fruit development from set to maturity. Longest stage. Fruits grow rapidly. High potassium demand.

fruit_set.description: Ovary swelling, petal fall, small green fruit visible

fruit_development.description: Rapid cell division and expansion. Fruit turns from green to straw-yellow.

fruit_maturation.description: Color development. Rind hardens. Sugar accumulation. Aril color deepens.

fruiting.irrigation: Full — 25-30 L/tree/day. Consistent moisture critical to prevent cracking.

secondary: Calcium Chloride 1% spray every 15 days (prevents cracking)
fertilizer.notes: High potassium for fruit sizing and sugar accumulation. Calcium prevents fruit cracking — the #1 quality problem.

harvest_ready.description: Fruit approaching harvest maturity. Color fully developed. Reduce fertilizer and water to improve sugar concentration and storage life.
visual_cues: Minor rind cracking in over-mature fruit
harvest_ready.irrigation: Reduce to 10-12 L/tree/day — 15 days before harvest

fertilizer.avoid: AVOID nitrogen — delays maturity, reduces sugar, promotes vegetative flush
fertilizer.notes: Minimal fertigation. Focus on color and sugar.

harvest_ready.robot_action: DOSE — minimal potassium only. Flag harvest-ready for picking team.

post_harvest.description: After fruit removal. Recovery feeding before next bahar treatment.
post_harvest.irrigation: Maintain 15-20 L/tree/day until stress period begins

fertilizer.notes: Replenish tree reserves. Apply FYM/compost to basin. Last chance before rest.

post_harvest.robot_action: DOSE — balanced NPK + flag for FYM application by field crew

bacterial_blight.prevalence: Most devastating disease of pomegranate in India — can destroy 60-80% of crop
visual_symptoms: Oily water-soaked spots on leaves (early)
Dark brown to black irregular lesions on leaves
L-shaped or Y-shaped cracking on fruit rind
Cankers on twigs and branches
Gummy exudate from infected bark
Premature fruit drop
bacterial_blight.favorable_conditions: High humidity >80%, temperatures 25-35°C, monsoon season, dense canopy

chemical: Streptomycin sulfate 500 ppm + Copper oxychloride 2.5 g/L
cultural: Prune and burn infected branches (10-15 cm below canker)
Open canopy by thinning — improve air circulation
Avoid mrig bahar in endemic areas — switch to ambe/hasta bahar
Sanitize pruning tools with 1% sodium hypochlorite

bacterial_blight.robot_decision: If bacterial_blight is flagged: REJECT dosing (liquid on wet canopy spreads inoculum). Log severity. Alert operator. Skip tree.

visual_symptoms: Small circular dark brown spots on leaves (2-5 mm)
Yellow halo around spots
Premature defoliation in severe cases
cercospora_leaf_spot.robot_decision: ALLOW dosing but log disease flag. Recommend fungicide spray to operator.

visual_symptoms: Black heart — internal fruit rot not visible outside
Slight discoloration at calyx end
Fruit feels lighter than normal
Cut fruit shows brown-black aril decay
alternaria_fruit_rot.robot_decision: ALLOW dosing. Log suspicion. Cannot detect black heart from camera — flag for manual inspection.

visual_symptoms: Small dark sunken spots on fruit rind
Spots enlarge with concentric rings
Pinkish-orange spore masses in wet weather
Leaf blight with irregular brown patches
Sudden wilting of one or more branches
Brown discoloration of vascular tissue (cut stem to check)
Complete tree death in 2-3 weeks if untreated
Gummy exudate from trunk base

chemical: Carbendazim 2 g/L soil drench (early stage only)
cultural: Remove and burn dead trees immediately
Do not replant in same pit for 2 years

wilt.robot_decision: If wilt detected: REJECT dosing. Mark tree as DEAD/DYING. Alert operator IMMEDIATELY. High priority.

fruit_cracking.cause: Physiological — not pathogen. Caused by irregular irrigation, calcium deficiency, or sudden rain after drought.
visual_symptoms: Longitudinal or radial cracks on fruit rind
Exposed arils attract secondary infections and fruit flies

preventive: Consistent drip irrigation — no drought-then-flood cycles
CaCl2 1% spray every 15 days from fruit set
GA3 (Gibberellic acid) 25 ppm spray at pea stage

fruit_cracking.robot_decision: ALLOW dosing. Add calcium to dose if cracking detected. Log severity.

fruit_borer.organism: Deudorix (Virachola) isocrates (Anar Butterfly / Pomegranate Fruit Borer)
fruit_borer.description: Most serious pest. Larva bores into developing fruit through calyx. Causes fruit rot, secondary fungal infection, and total fruit loss.
visual_symptoms: Entry hole near calyx end (covered with frass)
Frass (excrement) on fruit surface
Fruit becomes soft, discolored
Adult butterflies hovering near flowers/young fruits

cultural: Calyx-end bagging of fruits after fruit set

fruit_borer.robot_decision: ALLOW dosing. Log pest flag. Alert for pest management spray schedule.

visual_symptoms: White cottony masses on twigs, leaves, fruits
Sooty mold on honeydew deposits
Stunted growth, leaf curling
mealybug.robot_decision: ALLOW dosing. Log pest flag. Avoid excess nitrogen (feeds mealybug population).

visual_symptoms: Scarring and russeting on fruit rind
Silvery streaks on young leaves
Curling and browning of leaf margins
Bore holes in trunk and thick branches
Sawdust-like frass at bore holes
Wilting of branches above bore site

chemical: Inject Dichlorvos 76% EC (5 ml/L) into bore hole + seal with mud
cultural: Apply lime + copper sulfate paste to trunk

stem_borer.robot_decision: ALLOW dosing but flag trunk damage. Alert operator.

annual_requirement_per_tree.note: For a mature bearing tree (4+ years), drip-fertigated

visual: Uniform yellowing (chlorosis) of older leaves first
Marginal leaf scorch (brown edges) on older leaves
potassium.correction: Sulphate of Potash (SOP) 5 g/L or MKP 0:52:34 fertigation

calcium.correction: Calcium Nitrate 0.5% foliar spray + CaCl2 1% at fruit development

visual: Interveinal chlorosis on new/young leaves (green veins, yellow lamina)
iron.correction: FeSO4 0.5% foliar or Fe-EDDHA chelate in drip

boron.correction: Borax 0.2% spray at flowering and fruit set stage

fertigation_schedule_bhagwa.note: Split across growth stages via drip. Adjust for soil test results.

ideal_soil.CaCO3_pct: <15% (high lime locks up iron and zinc)

water_requirement.drip_recommendation: 2 drippers x 4 L/hr per tree, 2-4 hours/day depending on stage

climate_and_weather.ideal_climate: Semi-arid to subtropical; hot dry summers with cool winters produce best fruit color and sweetness.

temperature_c.dormancy_cold_tolerance: Tolerates down to -5 C when dormant, but active shoots/flowers injured below 0 C
temperature_c.heat_sunburn_threshold: >42 C causes fruit sun-scorch (use kaolin clay 3% spray or shade netting)

climate_and_weather.rainfall_mm: 500-750 mm/year ideal; >1000 mm or heavy monsoon rain during flowering/fruiting triggers severe bacterial blight and fruit cracking.
climate_and_weather.humidity: Low-to-moderate relative humidity (40-65%) ideal; >80% RH favors Xanthomonas bacterial blight and Cercospora.
climate_and_weather.sunlight: Full sun (>=6-8 hours/day) required for red aril/rind color and high Brix.

orchard_establishment_and_pruning.planting_season: Jul-Aug (monsoon onset) or Feb-Mar (spring, with assured drip irrigation).
orchard_establishment_and_pruning.propagation: Hardwood/semi-hardwood cuttings (15-20 cm, IBA 2000 ppm) or air-layering (gootee) from disease-free mother plants.
orchard_establishment_and_pruning.spacing_m: 4.5 x 3.0 m (740 trees/ha) or 4.0 x 2.5 m (1000 trees/ha) high-density; pit size 60 x 60 x 60 cm filled with topsoil + 20 kg FYM + Trichoderma.
orchard_establishment_and_pruning.training_system: Multi-stem bush (3-4 main stems per plant) — safer against stem borer/wilt than single-stem.
orchard_establishment_and_pruning.pruning: Light annual pruning after harvest/rest to remove water shoots, dead/diseased wood, and open center canopy for airflow and sunlight.

robot_decision_rules.description: Hard-coded rules the SLM must enforce in every decision.

rules.rule: NEVER dose during rest_pruning stage — tree is dormant
NEVER dose if bacterial_blight is detected — liquid spreads inoculum
NEVER dose if wilt is detected — tree may be dying
NEVER dose if tree was already dosed today (same crop_id)
During flowering: use P+K fertilizer ONLY — NO nitrogen
During fruiting: add calcium spray recommendation if fruit_cracking detected
Max dose 500 mL per tree per application
If fruit_borer detected: allow dosing but flag for pest management
If health_score < 0.3: skip dosing, flag for manual expert inspection
Adjust dose by growth stage: use the stage-specific protocol from dosing_protocols
If >3 consecutive trees skipped in a row: alert operator — possible systemic issue

flowering.notes: Promote fruit set. ZERO nitrogen. Boron critical.

fruiting.notes: Fruit sizing. High potassium. Add calcium spray.

harvest_ready.notes: Color and sugar. Minimal input. No nitrogen.

post_harvest.notes: Replenish reserves. Last window before rest.

default.notes: General maintenance — when growth stage is unknown.
